full_judgment: 3. The learned Munsif, on evidence adduced before him, found that the holding was an occupancy raiyati holding and accordingly he allowed both the cases for pre-emption. The learned District Judge, on appeal, set aside the judgment and order of the learned Munsifand dismissed those cases and disallowed pre-emption on a finding that the holding was a Korfa (under-raiyati) holding with occupancy right and that pre-emption under section 26F of the B. T. Act was not available. Thereafter the respondents, i.e., the pre-emptors, obtained two Rules. A learned Single Judge of the Dacca High Court made the Rules absolute on a finding that the Korfa (under-raiyati tenancy) under pre-emption was "upgraded to a raiyati tenancy since 14.4.56 as the rent-receiving interests of  the immediate landlord, who was a raiyat, stood acquired with effect from 14.4.56 under general Notification under section 3 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. He further found that section 26F of the B. T. Act was fully applicable to these cases as the sale took place on 4.12.1959 and, 5.12.1959 and the applications for pre-emption were filed on 3.12.1962 when B. T. Act was in force and was still governing the field.
